summary:
Binaural Earth Atlas is an interactive Earth observation and 3D spatial sonification web application built with React, TypeScript, D3, and the Web Audio API. It translates NASA GIBS satellite imagery and live NOAA geomagnetic telemetry into a synchronized 360-degree binaural soundscape alongside an interactive 3D orthographic globe and 2D Plate Carrée map.

Planetary datasets are often confined to static charts that obscure simultaneous environmental shifts and exclude blind or low-vision audiences. To address this, the platform extracts a six-signal feature vector—brightness, hue, saturation, edge density, frame motion, and climate anomaly—from four cardinal planetary streams (Cryosphere, Hydrosphere, Thermal, and Biosphere). These signals dynamically drive Web Audio HRTF spatial panning, relativistic Doppler pitch shifts, granular wind audio, auroral chimes, D3 thermal anomaly heatmaps, and swirling storm-radar pressure contours.

By unifying real-time geospatial visualization, accessible keyboard/speech controls, and responsive mobile touch interaction, Binaural Earth Atlas transforms complex climate telemetry into an intuitive, inclusive multisensory instrument.
details:
1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

Binaural Earth Atlas is an interactive Earth observation and 3D spatial sonification web observatory. It ingests real satellite imagery and space-weather telemetry, analyzes visual changes pixel-by-pixel in real time, and translates planetary dynamics into both an interactive multi-layer geospatial map and a 360-degree binaural soundscape.

How it works end-to-end:

  1. Multi-Stream Satellite Ingestion: Fetches EPSG:4326 WMTS tiles from NASA GIBS across four cardinal planetary domains—North (000°) Cryosphere Sea Ice (MODIS Terra), East (090°) Hydrosphere Chlorophyll-A (MODIS Aqua), South (180°) Thermal Sea Surface Temperature (GHRSST MUR L4), and West (270°) Biosphere Vegetation (MODIS NDVI)—alongside live geomagnetic Kp index data from NOAA SWPC.
    • Brightness → Pitch octave register
    • Hue Angle → Quantized musical scale degree (Pentatonic, Dorian, Harmonic)
    • Saturation → Lowpass filter brightness (400–6000 Hz)
    • Edge Density → Rhythmic pulse subdivisions (1× / 2× / 3×)
    • Frame Motion → Archive sequencer cadence (1500–2500 ms) & relativistic Doppler pitch shift
    • Climate Anomaly (>2σ) → Detuned harmonic tension blend
  2. 3D HRTF Spatial Sound Engine: Uses the Web Audio API (PannerNode with HRTF panning) to position the four Earth layers around the listener’s head (000°, 090°, 180°, 270°), enriched with granular wind synthesis, deterministic 2.8s planetary convolution reverb, auroral chimes, and solar flare noise sweeps.
  3. Synchronized Geospatial Viewport & Telemetry: Renders an interactive 3D Orthographic Globe and 2D EPSG:4326 Plate Carrée map with Wind Flow streamlines, UTC Solar Terminators, a D3 Climate Anomaly Heatmap (ΔT °C), D3 Storm Radar swirling pressure contours, a live FFT oscilloscope, Pearson correlation (r) scatter plot, and temporal trend charts.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Simultaneous Multi-Variable Perception: Human hearing excels at tracking subtle changes in pitch, timbre, rhythm, and spatial direction at once—allowing users to hear how sea-ice retreat, ocean blooms, thermal spikes, and vegetation shifts interact across seasons (2007, 2025, and 2026).
  • Accessibility & Inclusion: Designed with WCAG keyboard navigation (Space, ←/→, 1–4, single-key toggles), ARIA live telemetry announcements, and optional Web Speech narration with automatic audio ducking—making orbital climate telemetry genuinely explorable for blind and low-vision users.
  • Zero-Install Cross-Device Reach: Runs natively inside modern desktop and mobile web browsers with touch-ergonomic globe rotation, tap-to-probe telemetry, and six selectable color themes (including low-glare Night Mode and high-contrast Solar Flare).
  • Offline Resilience: Automatic fallback layers and a deterministic procedural Earth coastline model ensure the app remains functional even when external satellite endpoints are unreachable.

3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

Our goal is to democratize Earth science and foster deeper emotional and analytical engagement with climate telemetry. By bridging scientific accuracy with human spatial perception, Binaural Earth Atlas serves:

  • Educators & Students: As an interactive classroom laboratory comparing landmark climate shifts (such as the September 2007 Arctic sea-ice minimum) against contemporary 2025–2026 conditions.
  • Blind, Low-Vision & Neurodivergent Learners: Offering an equitable, non-visual-first pathway into NASA Earth observation datasets.
  • Researchers & Storytellers: Providing a rapid exploratory lens for spotting thermal/albedo correlations (Brightness vs. Climate Anomaly) and presenting planetary change in museum installations, science outreach, and public media.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Languages: TypeScript, TSX, HTML5, CSS3
  • Frontend & UI Framework: React 19, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide React
  • Geospatial & Scientific Visualization: D3 v7 (orthographic projections, thermal heatmaps, storm-radar contours, Pearson scatter plot), TopoJSON Client + world-atlas land geometry, Chart.js (temporal trend curves), HTML5 Canvas 2D
  • Audio & Accessibility Engines: Native Web Audio API (AudioContext, PannerNode HRTF, BiquadFilterNode, ConvolverNode, DynamicsCompressorNode, AnalyserNode), Web Speech API (speechSynthesis), ARIA Live Regions
  • Open Space Data APIs: NASA GIBS WMTS (gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov), NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (services.swpc.noaa.gov)
  • Hardware & Runtime Target: Standard developer workstations and consumer desktops, laptops, smartphones, and stereo headphones (for optimal binaural HRTF perception) running any modern Chromium, Firefox, or Safari browser.

5. How Is Your Project Creative?

Instead of treating audio as passive background music or simply reading chart numbers aloud, Binaural Earth Atlas builds an auditory spatial compass around the Earth:

  • Planetary Compass Spatialization: Turning your heading (000°–359°) physically rotates your acoustic perspective among Cryosphere, Hydrosphere, Thermal, and Biosphere streams—just like standing at the center of Earth’s coupled climate systems.
  • Physics-Inspired Sonification: Incorporates relativistic Doppler pitch shifts driven by frame-to-frame satellite motion, Magnetic Snap detents that gently pull toward high-anomaly sectors, and live Solar Wind / Kp triggers that inject metallic auroral chimes or noise bursts during geomagnetic storms.
  • Scientific Instrument Aesthetic: Pairs zero-radius technical geometry, monospace tabular telemetry, swirling D3 barometric storm isobars, and custom observatory themes (Obsidian, Aurora, Amber, Abyssal, Solar Flare, Night) so visual and acoustic feedback behave as one cohesive instrument.

6. What Factors Did Your Team Consider?

  • Data Reliability & Latency: Satellite WMTS tiles can be slow or rate-limited; we built in-memory frame caching, multi-tier fallback layers, abort timeouts on NOAA Kp polling, and procedural TopoJSON synthesis so playback never stalls.
  • Audio Comfort & Hearing Safety: Uncontrolled oscillators can sound harsh or clip; we routed every synth through biquad lowpass filtering, a DynamicsCompressorNode, voice-ducking during spoken telemetry, and smooth exponential crossfades (500 ms / EMA smoothing).
  • Color Contrast & Visual Ergonomics: Every theme—including red-shifted Night Mode for dark-adapted rooms and high-contrast Solar Flare—was tuned for clear hierarchy across DOM controls, SVG charts, and overlaid Canvas/D3 layers.
  • Mobile & Touch Ergonomics: On narrow viewports (360px+), dragging a 3D globe or compass can accidentally scroll the page; we engineered touch-action: none drag capture, >3px drag-vs-tap discrimination for mobile coordinate probing, responsive grid wrapping, and larger coarse-pointer slider targets.
  • Zero-Backend Portability & Privacy: Keeping all computation and localStorage preferences on the client eliminates server costs, accounts, or tracking while preserving instant deployment anywhere.
